request: Create a round-robin arbiter for four requesters.
expected_behavior: RTL for module rr_arbiter (N 4 by default) with ports clk rst_n req grant, a combinational same-cycle grant, and a pointer that moves to one past the winner, so no requester waits more than N-1 grants; with a self-checking testbench, gated by lint, simulation, and synthesis (and formal, when a .sby is written) before review.
constraints: Work only from the approved interface specification and microarchitecture.
Correct for an N that is not a power of two.
Lint-clean under Verilator -Wall with no waivers.
known_failure_modes: The winner keeps top priority (fixed priority, not round robin).
The pointer advancing when nothing was granted.
More than one grant, or a grant with no request.
A self-written testbench that never has everyone requesting; the held-out reference testbench judges instead.
A self-written testbench that cannot tell a starving or non-wrapping arbiter from a fair one; the must-fail control fails it.

held_out.name: The reference testbench passes on the seat's RTL
The seat's testbench fails each arbitration mutant
The case's N 5 proof reaches every cover and fails each mutant
The case's N 4 proof reaches every cover and fails each mutant wrong at N 4
